events.title: Pope John XXII condemns writings of Meister Eckhart as heretical
events.description: Pope John XXII condemned many writings of Meister Eckhart as heretical in the papal bull In Agro Dominico. Eckhart was a German priest, theologian, philosopher and mystic of the Dominican Order.
events.html: Pope John XXII condemned many writings of Meister Eckhart as heretical in the papal bull In Agro Dominico. Eckhart was a German priest, theologian, philosopher and mystic of the Dominican Order.

events.title: Juan Ponce de León sights Florida
events.description: Sailing north from Puerto Rico, Ponce de León sighted the coast he named La Florida, as it was the Easter season. He landed days later, beginning Spanish claims to the region.
events.html: Sailing north from Puerto Rico, Ponce de León sighted the coast he named La Florida, as it was the Easter season. He landed days later, beginning Spanish claims to the region.

events.title: Charles I becomes king on the death of James I
events.description: James I died at Theobalds and his son succeeded him. Charles's clashes with Parliament over money and religion led to civil war and his execution in 1649.
events.html: James I died at Theobalds and his son succeeded him. Charles's clashes with Parliament over money and religion led to civil war and his execution in 1649.

events.title: The Marquess of Rockingham forms his second British ministry
events.description: Charles Watson-Wentworth, 2nd Marquess of Rockingham, took office in Great Britain at the head of a ministry that began negotiations to end the American War of Independence. His second premiership lasted four months.
events.html: Charles Watson-Wentworth, 2nd Marquess of Rockingham, took office in Great Britain at the head of a ministry that began negotiations to end the American War of Independence. His second premiership lasted four months.

events.title: Congress passes the Naval Act, founding the US Navy
events.description: Prompted by Barbary corsairs seizing American ships, Congress authorised six frigates. Among them was USS Constitution, still in commission today.
events.html: Prompted by Barbary corsairs seizing American ships, Congress authorised six frigates. Among them was USS Constitution, still in commission today.

events.title: Scotland and England play the first rugby international
events.description: At Raeburn Place in Edinburgh, Scotland beat England by a goal and a try to a try before about 4,000 spectators. It was the first international rugby match.
events.html: At Raeburn Place in Edinburgh, Scotland beat England by a goal and a try to a try before about 4,000 spectators. It was the first international rugby match.

events.title: Two jumbo jets collide at Tenerife
events.description: A KLM 747 began its take-off in fog and struck a Pan Am 747 on the runway at Los Rodeos airport, killing 583 people. It remains the deadliest accident in aviation history.

events.title: Mount St Helens erupts for the first time in 123 years
events.description: A steam explosion blasted a crater in the summit of the Washington volcano after a week of earthquakes. On 18 May a massive eruption tore away its north face and killed 57 people.
events.html: A steam explosion blasted a crater in the summit of the Washington volcano after a week of earthquakes. On 18 May a massive eruption tore away its north face and killed 57 people.
